newsitem.title: UK: UK unions want to minimise strikes, no Labour deal.
newsitem.headline: UK unions want to minimise strikes, no Labour deal.

text.p: Britain's trade unions on Wednesday endorsed a strategy calling for social partnership between organised labour and employers, but union leaders denied they had done a deal to help out the opposition Labour Party in coming parliamentary elections.
The document, "Partners for Progress", calls for employers and unions to work together to solve problems in the field of employment, in particular in training.

John Monks, head of the Trade Unions Congress (TUC) that acts as a union umbrella group, told reporters the strategy document was not a deal but a paper that spelled out a "social partnership between unions and employers, involving the government".
"It's not a matter of 'putting a lid on strikes', but a genuine effort to minimise disputes, to avoid strikes, using arbitration, mediation and conciliation," Monks added.
"Inherent in the social partnership model outlined in this report is the need to minimise industrial disputes," the strategy document said.
Britain's main financial daily, The Financial Times, called the document a pledge by the TUC to limit strikes, "to reduce (the unions') potential to embarrass a future Labour government".
Labour is running strongly ahead of the ruling Conservatives in opinion surveys of voting intions in the next elections, which must be held by late May.
The last time that Labour held power in the 1970s, an upsurge of strikes made the unions very unpopular.
Monks denied the TUC had put its weight behind a minimum wage of four pounds ($6.55) an hour, but he said this was a long-standing aim for union negotiators in bargaining with employers.
The TUC's annual conference last September voted, against Monks' wishes, for a national minimum wage of 4.26 pounds an hour, but Monks said the TUC had yet to make a precise demand.
"We will name our bid after the election, when we're asked to, by a low pay commission," he said.

The Labour Party has pledged to bring in a national minimum wage if it wins the election after appointing a commission with members from the unions and employer groups to advise on the level. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
